title: NASA Activates 300‑MP Camera of Roman Space Telescope
seoTitle: NASA activates 300‑MP camera of Roman Telescope
subtitle: The 300‑megapixel infrared camera of the space telescope has been activated, bringing it closer to scientific operations in 2027.
excerpt: NASA successfully turned on the Roman Space Telescope’s 300‑megapixel infrared camera, which will capture vast swaths of the cosmos with Hubble‑like clarity, paving the way for science operations starting in 2027.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The American space agency (NASA) took a major step in readying the Roman Space Telescope by successfully activating its massive 300‑megapixel infrared camera. This is a pivotal moment for the observatory as it prepares for a phase of scientific operations dedicated to cosmic exploration. The camera, with its high resolution, is designed to capture vast stretches of the cosmos with clarity comparable to Hubble.

The primary role of this powerful infrared camera is to observe extensive regions of space. Infrared cameras are essential in modern astronomy because they detect light at wavelengths invisible to the human eye, which is crucial for penetrating cosmic dust clouds and viewing celestial objects that emit little visible light or lie at great distances. The ability to cover enormous portions of the cosmos means Roman can map large sky areas, revealing structures and phenomena.

In addition to the main camera activation, the Roman Telescope’s coronagraph, designed for planet hunting, is also functioning as expected. A coronagraph is a specialized instrument that blocks the intense glare of a central star, allowing astronomers to directly observe much fainter objects orbiting it, such as exoplanets. This capability is vital to Roman’s mission, opening the path for detecting and studying worlds beyond our solar system.

The successful activation of both the 300‑megapixel infrared camera and the coronagraph marks a significant advance for the Roman Space Telescope. These milestones bring the observatory closer to commencing its scientific operations. The expectation is that Roman will begin collecting valuable data and carrying out its scheduled observations starting in 2027, heralding a new era of discoveries in the study of the universe and the search for new worlds.

With information from ScienceDaily.
